desks.Dividends: Microsoft, ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter (pay Dec 10), is the only declared watchlist ex-date in the window, its 24th consecutive annual increase. Apple's dividend is still undeclared: a Nov 10 listing is a projection, not a declaration, with declaration watch on the Nov 2 earnings print. Nvidia, SPY and QQQ point to December on pattern only, Tesla pays no dividend, and no cuts or specials were found among watchlist names. The verified Oct 30 non-watchlist pile-up includes COST $1.47, TXN $1.52 on a roughly 7% raise, MS $1.15, EPD $0.56, PAA and PAGP $0.4175, O $0.2715, ZTS $0.53 and TRGP $1.25.
desks.Earnings: Amazon and Intel report tonight after close (calls 5:00 p.m. ET). Amazon's options-implied move is about 7.8-8.0% and Intel's about 9.2-9.3%, below Intel's 12.2% average over its last four reports. Intel's EPS consensus basis is UNVERIFIED: Nasdaq shows $0.28 while secondary previews cite an adjusted $0.39-0.40. Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close. Microsoft beat Oct 28 after close: revenue $92.3 billion (+19%), non-GAAP EPS $4.89 vs $4.71 consensus, Azure +48%. Alphabet's Oct 28 figures remain secondary-sourced; the primary release has still not been opened.
desks.Futures: EIA natural gas storage printed +80 Bcf for the week ended Oct 23, to 3,724 Bcf, above a roughly 70 Bcf survey estimate and the 77 Bcf five-year average; gas settled down 2.6% at $2.952 per MMBtu into warmer-than-usual forecasts. Crude eased Thursday on reports of revived US-Iran talks, with WTI down about 1% to $101.74, after Wednesday's rally. Sunday Nov 1 pairs a review-only OPEC+ meeting with Iran's Sinokor enforcement deadline, against October's record attack tempo and an unverified Oct 29 mine claim; UKMTO confirmed at least one vessel on fire. No new WASDE today; the October WASDE remains the grains anchor.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for the watchlist this week. The methodology item to watch is the S&P Dow Jones Indices growth/value revamp, effective at the annual reconstitution before the open Dec 21, 2026, with pro-forma files Dec 4: value scoring adds intangibles-adjusted book value and free-cash-flow-to-price, and 12-month price momentum drops from growth ranking. The cited $375 billion or more in passive funds tied to affected style benchmarks is an analyst estimate, not an S&P figure, and the change reclassifies style-index membership, not S&P 500 headline membership.
desks.Premium: Clean, usable implied-volatility reads exist for three names from post-close marks: Microsoft 28.4% for Oct 30, Tesla 26.1% and Nvidia 21.8%, with the latter two indicative only against a stale realized window ending Oct 27. Apple's only clean read is the Nov 4 earnings expiry at 36.8%. SPY and QQQ have no clean at-the-money implied volatility from post-close 1-day marks, with call-put gaps of 15 and 43 percentage points; their put legs alone are not at-the-money volatility. Microsoft's volatility fell from 61.4% before its print to 28.4% after the beat, still above 20.1% realized. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names.
desks.Quant lab: No new candidates today and nothing appended to the ledger, deliberately: the ledger already contains a complete Oct 29 sweep (rows #170-181), and re-running it would duplicate those rows. The sweep's only TEST candidate is #171 darm-vol (score 66), a packaged conditional-volatility model set; WATCH candidates are #170 (score 64), an honest-negative LSTM-vs-HAR result, and #179 (score 48), a Hawkes feed-hygiene note. The Oct 28-29 arXiv window is genuinely empty in the announcement mirror, with the newest announcement still Oct 27. No INTEGRATE movement.

headline: Daily research brief — Thursday, October 29

items.detail: Amazon reports tonight after close with an options-implied move of about 7.8-8.0% (about $20.27 on the TipRanks estimate), and Intel reports tonight with about 9.2-9.3% priced, below its 12.2% average realized move over the last four quarters. Intel's EPS consensus cannot be quoted as a single number: Nasdaq shows $0.28 while secondary previews cite an adjusted $0.39-0.40, and which basis matches the print is UNVERIFIED. Apple's cleaner avoid is Monday Nov 2: the Nov 4 straddle implies about 3.9% against a 2.3% average realized move over the last 12 reports, with Nov 4 implied volatility at a clean 36.8%.
items.title: Tonight is the binary: Amazon about 8%, Intel about 9%

items.detail: The Fed held Oct 28 at 3.75-4.00% on a 10-2 vote with no September PCE in hand, and the data arrived this morning: Q3 GDP advanced 3.4% annualized, above consensus of about 3.1-3.2%, and September PCE rose 3.6% year over year headline and 3.1% core, with the monthly pace re-accelerating even as the quarterly PCE price index eased to 2.1%. These prints are secondary-corroborated, not read directly from the BEA, so they are UNVERIFIED against the primary source. December stays live, with no single probability quoted because recent secondary reads disagree.
items.title: The Fed decided without the data; the data came in hot on growth

items.detail: FRED prints dated Oct 28 put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.67% and the 10-year at 5.05%, a 2s10s spread of +38 basis points after a 9-point decision-day re-steepening, with SOFR 6 basis points over the effective fed funds rate. Funding is calm and the curve is upward-sloping, but the 10-year back above 5% is a valuation headwind for long-duration names such as Nvidia, Tesla and Microsoft on discount-rate grounds. The day's move was long-end-led, reading as term-premium and inflation compensation rising rather than a near-term policy-path repricing.
items.title: Rates: 10-year above 5%, curve steeper, funding calm

items.detail: Sunday Nov 1 is the futures desk's live risk: a review-only OPEC+ meeting collides with the Persian Gulf Strait Authority's Sinokor enforcement deadline, against October's record attack tempo, 11 VLCCs hit in October alone, and an unverified Oct 29 claim that three tankers struck sea mines, with UKMTO confirming at least one vessel on fire. Crude's premium is sticky: Thursday's roughly $1 pullback came out of the headline tail, not the base. Natural gas is the mirror image: a bearish +80 Bcf storage print into a warm start to heating season. Quote Hormuz flows as a range, never a point.
items.title: Sunday Nov 1: OPEC+ review meets the Sinokor deadline
